target_customer: Bay Area homeowners with a backyard who want an ADU built with no upfront cost, later homebuilders and developers
problem: Housing construction is slow and artisan driven; ADU rules had loosened but building a backyard unit was costly and slow for owners.
business_model: Revenue share on rental income from factory built ADUs, later contracted homebuilding

founders.name: Brian Bakerman
education: Carnegie Mellon University, B.S. Electrical and Computer Engineering
previous_startups: AI transcription startup (sold, per YC page)

founders.name: Spencer Burleigh
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as an engineer and the founder of Rent the Backyard. ABC7 and Dwell 2019 coverage name both founders.

exit.reason: Co-founder wrote that the factory had high fixed costs, the company was undercapitalized, and venture debt, inventory and receivables financing were refused.

competitors.name: United Dwelling
competitors.what: Places affordable backyard units in exchange for a share of rent

competitors.name: OBY Cooperative
competitors.what: Turnkey prefab ADUs in the East Bay

technical_complexity.rationale: Offsite construction with a factory, permitting and logistics; hard for a small team but using known methods.

defensibility.rationale: Factory scale could help but customers had low switching costs and others offered the same no cost model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it; the company closed in December 2022 after failing to raise debt.

market_need_then: California eased ADU permitting in 2017 to 2019 and the Bay Area had a severe housing shortage; ABC7 and Dwell covered the launch in 2019.

branding.name_origin: Pippin was the later parent brand; no source explains the name. Rent the Backyard was the consumer brand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain consumer pitch: a home in your backyard for free

rebrands.why: YC page shows Pippin as the parent brand with Rent the Backyard as its ADU brand; date not sourced

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the launch by ABC7, Dwell and Planetizen in 2019.

brand_strength.rationale: Several outlets covered the launch, but no evidence of a brand driven community.

pivots.from: Rent the Backyard, no cost ADUs for homeowners
pivots.to: Pippin, autonomous homebuilding factory for duplexes and apartments
pivots.why: Positioning on the YC page; reason not sourced

outcome_analysis: Rent the Backyard launched in 2019 to build free ADUs in exchange for rental income and grew to a reported run rate above 10M dollars with about 10 homes built. The co-founder blog says high fixed factory costs and under capitalization hurt it, and lenders refused debt, so it shut down in December 2022 with customers refunded or delivered homes.
notes: No company website is listed; treated as dead. The shutdown post could not be opened (404 on fetch); its content is taken from a search summary of that URL, so cause details are secondhand. The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights, total 150K, Aug 2019); Dealroom shows 125K at 2.0M valuation, a conflict. Competitor dates are the year of the Dwell roundup, exact month not confirmed.
